clue.text: Demonstrate bit of skill — and how!

indicators.note: a bit of a word is just a small piece of it, here its opening letter

blocks.note: the opening letter of skill
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone being urged to display a little of their talent, with an enthusiastic 'and how!' cheering them on.
explanation.definitionFit: To show something is to demonstrate it, a plain synonym for displaying or exhibiting.

clue.text: Work hard on a new catchword

blocks.note: to slog is to toil away
taken as written
N is the standard abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: An advertising team toiling away to come up with a fresh catchword.
explanation.definitionFit: A catchword is a memorable phrase or motto used by a campaign, which is what a slogan is.

clue.text: The position lies unsettled, so declare war?

indicators.note: something unsettled is disturbed and out of place, so these letters must be shaken up into new order

blocks.note: all fifteen letters of these three words are the fodder

explanation.surface: A diplomatic standoff is so unstable that a nation might as well go to war.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks the definition as a loose equivalent: declaring war is one way to begin fighting openly.
explanation.definitionFit: To open hostilities is to begin armed fighting, which is what a declaration of war announces.

clue.text: Trainee astronaut, one who often gets high

blocks.note: first meaning: a cadet in training for space travel
second meaning: slang for a dreamy, spaced-out person, often from drugs

explanation.surface: A recruit training to fly into orbit, who naturally gets up very high.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gets high' reads as rocketing upward for an astronaut, but the second meaning is the drug sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally a cadet of space flight; informally a vague, absent-minded person, as if permanently intoxicated.

clue.text: Friend reportedly failed to see fortune-teller

indicators.note: a report is something heard, so the words are taken by their sound when spoken

blocks.note: a pal is a friend
failed to see means missed, which is said the same as a word for fog

explanation.surface: A friend apparently didn't foresee what was coming, despite being a fortune-teller.
explanation.definitionFit: A palmist tells fortunes by reading the lines on a person's hand.

clue.text: Business interest

blocks.note: first meaning: a company or firm
second meaning: a matter that affects or involves one

explanation.walkthrough: Read together it sounds like a commercial stake; the two words are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: A firm is a going concern, and something that interests or affects you is your concern.

clue.text: Talk about last to leave do

indicators.note: the last of a word is its final letter
about means surrounding, so one piece goes around the other

blocks.note: to chat is to talk
the final letter of leave

explanation.surface: Gossiping about who was last to depart a party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Do' looks like a party, but here it is the verb meaning swindle.
explanation.definitionFit: To do someone is informal British for swindling them, the same as to cheat them.

clue.text: Household skills demonstrated by servant since cooking course (not ours)

indicators.note: not ours tells us to take away that run of letters from the neighbouring word
cooking means mixing up, so the remaining letters are stirred into a new order

blocks.note: a domestic is a household servant
taken as written
taken as written, before the deletion

explanation.surface: A servant shows off home skills, having been on a cookery course that wasn't the speaker's.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not ours' strips four letters out of the word before it, leaving just two to mix. 'Cooking' sits neatly in a kitchen scene but signals the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Domestic science is the old school subject teaching cooking, cleaning and other household management.

clue.text: Parody attempt to conceal an undergarment

indicators.note: to conceal something is to hide it inside, so one piece wraps around the other

blocks.note: a try is an attempt
the indefinite article
a vest is a garment worn under a shirt

explanation.surface: A comic sketch where someone tries to hide their underwear.
explanation.definitionFit: A travesty is a grotesque or absurd imitation, i.e. a parody or mockery.

clue.text: Tumble on top of rest

blocks.note: over means above or on top of
the balance is the rest or remainder

explanation.surface: Someone falls over on top of whatever else is lying around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rest' suggests repose, but here it is the remainder, as in the balance of a bill.
explanation.definitionFit: To overbalance is to lose one's equilibrium and fall over, which is to tumble.

clue.text: Cheerful lad, we hear, followed by social worker

indicators.note: what we hear is spoken, so the word is taken for its sound rather than its spelling

blocks.note: a lad is a boy, which is pronounced like a floating marker at sea
ants are social insects, and the worker is one caste of the colony

explanation.surface: A happy young man with a social worker trailing behind him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Social worker' reads as a welfare professional, but it is a worker ant, ants being social insects.
explanation.definitionFit: Buoyant means light-hearted and optimistic, as if floating along in good spirits.

clue.text: Mother carrying one girl

indicators.note: carrying means holding within, so one piece goes inside the other

blocks.note: ma is an informal word for mother
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A mother holding her baby daughter.
explanation.definitionFit: Mia is a female first name, so it can stand for a girl in crossword convention.

clue.text: A Greek goddess paid her to in error

indicators.note: something in error is wrong or mistaken, so these letters are in the wrong order

blocks.note: the nine letters of these three words are the fodder

explanation.surface: Someone mistakenly handed money to a Greek goddess.
explanation.walkthrough: The opening 'A' belongs to the definition, not the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Aphrodite is the Greek goddess of love and beauty, an example of the class named.

clue.text: Head of security in art gallery gains experience

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter
gains means takes in, so the gallery holds the other piece inside it

blocks.note: the Tate is the famous London art gallery
the opening letter of security

explanation.surface: The head of security at an art gallery picks up some practical experience.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tate is the national gallery of British and modern art in London.
explanation.definitionFit: A taste of something is a brief experience of it, as in a taste of freedom.

clue.text: The place from which one begins a journey trainspotting, possibly

definitions.text: The place from which one begins a journey

indicators.note: possibly suggests one of several forms, so the letters may be arranged another way

blocks.note: the whole word is the fodder

explanation.surface: A train station platform, where a journey starts, might well be where trainspotters gather.
explanation.walkthrough: Trainspotting, the hobby of logging locomotives, fits a railway journey neatly.
explanation.definitionFit: A starting point is literally the place where a journey or process begins.

clue.text: Cement mostly used round about start of century to make a form of concrete

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the word loses its final letter
the start of a word is its first letter
round means surrounding, so the shortened word goes around the other pieces

blocks.note: paste is an adhesive, a cement, before shortening
re means about or concerning
the opening letter of century

explanation.surface: Instructions for a builder mixing cement into a particular kind of concrete.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cement' reads as building material but is clued as a glue: paste. Precast is a verb as well as an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: To precast concrete is to mould it into blocks or panels before putting it in place.

clue.text: In front of husband, rip page out showing inscription

indicators.note: out can mean disordered or not as it should be, so these letters are reorganised

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
H is the abbreviation for husband

explanation.surface: A wife tears a page from a book right in front of her husband, revealing a written dedication.
explanation.definitionFit: An epigraph is an engraved inscription on a building or statue, or a quotation heading a book.

clue.text: One employed in Fleet Street, running off pursued by crowd?

blocks.note: to run off copies is to print them
a press is a dense crowd or throng

explanation.surface: A Fleet Street journalist running away, chased by a mob.
explanation.walkthrough: Fleet Street in London was the home of the British newspaper industry; 'one employed' there sounds like a person but is a machine.
explanation.definitionFit: Printing presses were the machines used to produce newspapers in Fleet Street.

clue.text: Composer's new look

blocks.note: novel means new or original
lo is an old exclamation meaning look

explanation.surface: A musician has been given a fresh image makeover.
explanation.walkthrough: Ivor Novello was a Welsh composer and actor of the early twentieth century.
explanation.definitionFit: Ivor Novello wrote popular songs and musicals, so his surname identifies a composer.

clue.text: Lift beam across ring

indicators.note: lying across something spans it, so one piece goes either side of the other

blocks.note: a purlin is a horizontal roof beam
O is the shape of a ring

explanation.surface: A builder raising a beam over a circular frame.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lift' looks like raising, but it is slang for steal.
explanation.definitionFit: To lift something is informal for stealing it, and to purloin is to steal.

clue.text: Daughter, leaving study ahead of boy, makes an excuse

indicators.note: leaving means departing, so that letter goes out of the word

blocks.note: D is the abbreviation for daughter
to read a subject is to study it
a son is a boy

explanation.surface: A daughter abandons her studies before her brother and gives a justification.
explanation.definitionFit: A reason offered for one's conduct is a justification, much like an excuse.

clue.text: Laborious work, note, filling in crossword diagram

indicators.note: filling in means occupying a space inside, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: the grid is the pattern of squares in a crossword
N is the abbreviation for note

explanation.surface: The tedious task of writing answers into the squares of a crossword.
explanation.definitionFit: A grind is a monotonous, tiring task, like the daily drudgery of hard labour.

clue.text: Discharge leader of battalion after protest march

indicators.note: the leader of a word is the letter at its front
after places the battalion's letter second, behind the protest march rather than ahead of it

blocks.note: a demo is a protest march
the opening letter of battalion

explanation.surface: A battalion commander is dismissed following a protest march.
explanation.walkthrough: Demob is short for demobilise, releasing troops from service.
explanation.definitionFit: To demob a soldier is to discharge them from the armed forces at the end of service.

clue.text: Resourceful substitute almost checked by foul

indicators.note: almost means not quite complete, so the word drops its final letter
to be checked by something is to be held in by it, so one piece sits inside the other

blocks.note: vile means foul or disgusting
ersatz means substitute, before shortening

explanation.surface: A resourceful replacement footballer is nearly stopped by a foul tackle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Substitute' and 'foul' suggest football, but substitute is the adjective ersatz and foul is vile.
explanation.definitionFit: Versatile means adaptable to many uses or tasks, which is what a resourceful person is.

clue.text: Champion boxer from Australia

indicators.note: from signals that the letters are taken out of the next word

blocks.note: three letters inside the word

explanation.surface: A boxing champion who comes from Australia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'From Australia' sounds like a nationality, but the boxer is American and sits inside the word.
explanation.definitionFit: Muhammad Ali was world heavyweight boxing champion three times.

clue.text: Unhappy chappies make harsh criticisms, upon reflection, about subject matter

indicators.note: a reflection is a mirror image, so the word is turned back to front
about means surrounding, so one piece goes around the other

blocks.note: to slam is to criticise harshly
content is the subject matter of a work

explanation.surface: Discontented men tear into what a piece is about, then think again.
explanation.definitionFit: Malcontents are people who are dissatisfied and rebellious, chronically unhappy with things.

clue.text: Henry, with mum in new bar, has potato dish

indicators.note: new suggests a fresh form, so the word's letters are rearranged
in tells us one piece is placed inside the other

blocks.note: H is the symbol for the henry, the unit of inductance
taken as written, before rearranging
mum means silent, as in keep mum, and sh is the call for silence
to have something is to own it

explanation.surface: Henry and his mother eat potato dish at a newly opened bar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Has' looks like a link to the definition, but it is wordplay; 'mum' is not a mother but silence.
explanation.definitionFit: Hash browns are a dish of grated or chopped potato fried until crisp.

clue.text: Film director tucked into bubble-and-squeak

indicators.note: tucked into means placed inside, so the letters sit within the words that follow

blocks.note: found across the join of the first two parts

explanation.surface: A film director eating bubble-and-squeak, the British dish of fried leftover potato and cabbage.
explanation.walkthrough: Bubble-and-squeak is a British dish of fried leftover potato and cabbage. 'Tucked into' suggests eating.
explanation.definitionFit: David Lean directed Lawrence of Arabia and Brief Encounter, so his surname names a film director.
